questions.question: Which of the following was opened by Gour Mohan Addy in 1829 ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oriental Seminary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Oriental Seminary was founded by Gour Mohan Addy in 1829 in Kolkata.

• It was one of the first privately run, non-missionary schools in India.

• Unlike other contemporary institutions, Oriental Seminary was established to impart education that was not influenced by Christian missionaries.

• The school played a significant role in the Bengal Renaissance by providing quality education in English and Bengali.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Bengal Renaissance**

• The Bengal Renaissance was a cultural, social, intellectual, and artistic movement in Bengal, primarily in the city of Kolkata, during the 19th and early 20th centuries.

• It is considered to have begun with Raja Ram Mohan Roy in the early 19th century and continued with many notable figures like Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar and Swami Vivekananda.

• The movement was marked by a period of significant socio-cultural reform, including the promotion of education, the eradication of social evils, and the revival of literature and arts.

• **Gour Mohan Addy**

• Gour Mohan Addy was an Indian educationist and social reformer who played a pivotal role in the establishment of educational institutions in Bengal during the 19th century.

• He is best known for founding the Oriental Seminary, which became a model for many other private educational institutions in India.

• **Missionary Schools**

• Missionary schools were educational institutions established by Christian missionaries during the British colonial period in India.

• These schools aimed to spread Christianity and provide Western-style education to Indian students.

• They played a significant role in the spread of English education and Western knowledge in India.

• **Educational Reforms in 19th Century India**

• The 19th century saw several educational reforms in India, including the establishment of schools and colleges, the introduction of new curricula, and the promotion of English education.

• Notable figures like Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, and others contributed to these reforms, advocating for modern education and social change.

</ul

questions.question: In which pair of states is Holi also celebrated as Dola Purnima?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal and Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dola Purnima** is celebrated with great fervor in both **West Bengal and Odisha** during the festival of Holi.
 
• It is also known as **Dol Jatra** in these regions.
 
• The festival involves the worship of **Lord Krishna** and people participate in joyous processions carrying the idol of Krishna on decorated palanquins.
 
• It is marked by the **playing of colors**, singing, dancing, and various traditional rituals and customs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dola Purnima**

 
 
• Dola Purnima is celebrated on the full moon day in the month of Phalguna (February-March).
 
• It is a significant festival for the followers of Vaishnavism, a sect of Hinduism that worships Lord Vishnu and his incarnations, particularly Krishna.
 
• The festival signifies the arrival of spring and is also associated with agricultural activities, especially the harvesting of new crops.
 
• In Odisha, the festival includes a ritual known as **Melana**, where deities from various temples are brought together in a grand procession.
 
 
 
• **Holi**
 
 
• Holi is one of the major festivals of India and is celebrated with enthusiasm across the country.
 
• It is known as the "Festival of Colors" and signifies the victory of good over evil, the arrival of spring, and the end of winter.
 
• The festival is celebrated by smearing colors on each other, dancing, singing, and enjoying festive foods and drinks.
 
• Holi is celebrated over two days, starting with Holika Dahan (bonfire) on the night before and followed by the main day of playing with colors.

questions.question: Which political party was in power when Sardar Swaran Singh Committee made recommendations about Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian National Congress**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Sardar Swaran Singh Committee was constituted by the **Indian National Congress** government in 1976.

• It was formed during the tenure of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**.

• The committee was set up to study and make recommendations on **Fundamental Duties** to be included in the Indian Constitution.

• The recommendations of the committee led to the incorporation of **Fundamental Duties** in the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Fundamental Duties:**

• Fundamental Duties are a set of moral obligations for Indian citizens, which were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

• These duties are enshrined in Part IV-A of the Constitution under Article 51A.

• Initially, there were 10 Fundamental Duties, but the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added an 11th duty.

• These duties include respect for the Constitution, the national flag, and the national anthem, promoting harmony, and preserving the rich heritage of the composite culture.

• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**

• This amendment is often referred to as the "Mini-Constitution" due to the extensive changes it brought to the Indian Constitution.

• It was enacted during the Emergency period under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's government.

• Besides adding the Fundamental Duties, it also made significant changes to the Preamble and extended the duration of the Lok Sabha and State Legislatures from 5 to 6 years.

• The amendment aimed to reduce the power of the judiciary and strengthen the central government's authority.

• **Sardar Swaran Singh:**

• Sardar Swaran Singh was a prominent Indian politician and a senior leader of the Indian National Congress.

• He served as the Union Minister for various portfolios, including Defence, External Affairs, and Agriculture.

• He chaired the committee that recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution.

• His contributions to Indian politics and governance have been significant, especially during the formative years of independent India.

</ul

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution is related with promotion of co - operative societies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 43 B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Article 43 B was inserted into the Constitution of India by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011.

• This article is specifically aimed at promoting voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of co-operative societies.

• Co-operative societies are institutions that are voluntarily formed by individuals with common economic, social, and cultural needs and interests.

• Promotion of co-operative societies aims to enhance economic and social development, particularly in rural areas, by encouraging self-help and mutual aid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Article 31 B**

• Article 31 B of the Indian Constitution was introduced by the First Amendment in 1951.

• It provides protection to laws included in the Ninth Schedule from being challenged and invalidated on the ground of violation of fundamental rights.

• The Ninth Schedule was created to give effect to certain land reform measures and prevent them from being challenged in courts.

• **Article 51 A**

• Article 51 A specifies the Fundamental Duties of every citizen of India.

• These duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

• It includes duties such as respecting the national symbols, protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India, promoting harmony, and safeguarding public property.

• **Article 39 A**

• Article 39 A directs the State to provide free legal aid to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities.

• This article emphasizes the importance of equal justice and free legal aid.

• It was added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

</ul

questions.question: In 2016, Yamini Krishnamurthy received the Padma Vibhushan for her contribution to which fields of classical dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Yamini Krishnamurthy** is renowned for her exceptional proficiency in both Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dance forms.
 
• She has significantly contributed to the **preservation and promotion of classical dance** in India and internationally.
 
• Her performances are characterized by **grace, precision, and intense emotion** that resonate with audiences worldwide.
 
• In recognition of her immense contribution to Indian classical dance, she was awarded the **Padma Vibhushan** in 2016, India's second-highest civilian award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating from Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork, along with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions.
 
• Bharatanatyam has its roots in the **Natyashastra**, an ancient treatise on performing arts written by Bharata Muni.
 
• This dance form is traditionally performed by women and is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and spirituality.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**
 
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form that originated in Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• It is known for its graceful movements, fast rhythms, and dramatic storytelling.
 
• Like Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi also involves intricate footwork, hand gestures, and facial expressions to convey emotions and narratives.
 
• Kuchipudi performances often include both solo and group acts, and they traditionally start with a prayer to the gods.
 
 
 
• **Padma Vibhushan**
 
 
• The Padma Vibhushan is the second-highest civilian award in India, given for exceptional and distinguished service in any field.
 
• It was instituted in 1954 and is awarded to recognize excellence in various disciplines, including arts, public affairs, science, and engineering.
 
• The awardees receive a certificate signed by the President of India and a medallion.
 
• The Padma Vibhushan is part of the Padma Awards, which also include the Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.

questions.question: The number of white rooks used in chess is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a standard game of chess, each player starts with two rooks.
 
• The rooks are placed at the corners of the chessboard.
 
• The white rooks are initially placed on the squares a1 and h1.
 
• Rooks move horizontally or vertically any number of squares without jumping over other pieces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chessboard Setup:**

 
 
• A standard chessboard consists of 64 squares arranged in an 8x8 grid.
 
• Each player starts with 16 pieces: 1 king, 1 queen, 2 rooks, 2 knights, 2 bishops, and 8 pawns.
 
 
 
• **Rook Movement:**
 
 
• The rook can move horizontally or vertically through any number of unoccupied squares.
 
• It cannot jump over other pieces.
 
• The rook is a powerful piece, especially in the endgame when it can control open files and ranks.
 
 
 
• **Chess Strategies Involving Rooks:**
 
 
• Rooks are most effective when placed on open files or ranks where they can exert their power over a larger area of the board.
 
• Doubling rooks on a file (placing them one behind the other) increases their power and control.
 
• The rook and king work together effectively in the endgame to checkmate the opponent's king.

questions.question: As per Human Development Report 2021 - 22, what is the female Life Expectancy at birth in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**67.5 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Human Development Report 2021-22, the female life expectancy at birth in India is 67.5 years.
 
• Life expectancy at birth is the average number of years a newborn is expected to live if current mortality rates continue to apply.
 
• Increased life expectancy indicates improvements in healthcare, nutrition, and general living conditions.
 
• Life expectancy is a key indicator used to measure the overall health and well-being of a population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Report (HDR)**

 
 
• The Human Development Report is an annual report published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• It measures development not only through economic growth but also through improvements in health, education, and income.
 
• The HDR uses the Human Development Index (HDI) as a composite statistic of life expectancy, education, and per capita income indicators.
 
• Countries are ranked based on their HDI to assess their development progress.
 
 
 
• **Life Expectancy at Birth**
 
 
• It is an estimate of the average number of years a newborn is expected to live if current mortality rates remain constant throughout their life.
 
• Life expectancy is influenced by factors such as healthcare access, quality of life, and socio-economic conditions.
 
• Higher life expectancy typically correlates with better health care, nutrition, and overall living conditions.
 
• It is a crucial indicator for assessing the effectiveness of public health policies and socio-economic development.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Life Expectancy**
 
 
• Access to healthcare services and quality of medical care.
 
• Living conditions, including housing, sanitation, and nutrition.
 
• Social determinants such as education, income, and employment.
 
• Public health policies and preventative measures.

questions.question: When lava makes its way through cracks and fissures developed in the ground, it solidifies almost perpendicular to the ground. It cools down in the same position to develop a wall-like structure. What is this structure called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dykes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dykes** are geological structures formed when magma intrudes into pre-existing rock formations and solidifies.
 
• They are generally **vertical or steeply inclined** and cut across the bedding planes of the host rock.
 
• Dykes often form **wall-like structures** that are perpendicular to the ground surface.
 
• These formations are important indicators of **tectonic activity** and magma movement within the Earth's crust.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lacolith:**

 
 
• A laccolith is a type of igneous intrusion that has a dome-shaped upper surface and a flat floor.
 
• It forms when magma intrudes between two layers of sedimentary rock, causing the overlying strata to bulge upwards.
 
• Laccoliths are typically smaller than batholiths and have a lens-like shape.
 
 
 
• **Lapolith:**
 
 
• A lapolith is a large, lenticular, igneous intrusion that is concave downward.
 
• It forms when magma intrudes into the crust and then spreads out laterally in a dome-like fashion.
 
• Lapoliths can be associated with large-scale volcanic activity and often contain significant mineral deposits.
 
 
 
• **Phacolith:**
 
 
• A phacolith is a lens-shaped igneous intrusion that is typically found in the cores of anticlines or the troughs of synclines.
 
• It forms when magma intrudes into the fold structures of sedimentary rocks.
 
• Phacoliths are usually smaller than laccoliths and are associated with fold mountain belts.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT found in animal cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plastid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Plastids are not found in animal cells**. They are present only in plant cells and some protists.

• Plastids are responsible for photosynthesis, storage of products like starch, and synthesis of many types of molecules that are needed as cellular building blocks.

• There are different types of plastids, such as chloroplasts, chromoplasts, and leucoplasts, each serving different functions within the plant cell.

• Chloroplasts, a type of plastid, contain the pigment chlorophyll, which is essential for the process of photosynthesis in plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**

• The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a network of membranous tubules within the cytoplasm of a eukaryotic cell, continuous with the nuclear membrane.

• It usually has ribosomes attached and is involved in protein and lipid synthesis.

• There are two types of ER: Rough ER (with ribosomes) and Smooth ER (without ribosomes).

• Rough ER is involved in protein synthesis and quality control, while Smooth ER is associated with lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.

• **Mitochondria**

• Mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell as they generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.

• Mitochondria have their own DNA and are involved in various cellular processes including energy production, cellular differentiation, and apoptosis (cell death).

• They have a double membrane; the inner membrane is folded into cristae which increases the surface area for energy production.

• **Golgi Complex**

• The Golgi complex, also known as the Golgi apparatus or Golgi body, is an organelle found in most eukaryotic cells.

• It is composed of stacked membrane-bound sacs and is involved in the modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins for secretion or delivery to other organelles.

• The Golgi apparatus is often considered the "post office" of the cell, as it tags proteins with molecular markers to ensure they reach their correct destination.

</ul

questions.question: Which of the following Articles deals with the amendment of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 368**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 368 of the Indian Constitution deals with the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and its procedure.
 
• This article provides the procedure for the amendment of the Constitution, which can be initiated only by the introduction of a Bill for the purpose in either House of Parliament.
 
• The Bill must be passed in each House by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of that House present and voting.
 
• Some amendments require the additional ratification by at least one-half of the State Legislatures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 360**

 
 
• Article 360 empowers the President of India to proclaim a Financial Emergency if he/she believes that the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
 
• During Financial Emergency, the executive authority of the Union extends to the giving of directions to any State to observe such canons of financial propriety as may be specified in the directions, and such other measures as the President may deem necessary.
 
 
 
• **Article 352**
 
 
• Article 352 empowers the President to declare a National Emergency when the security of India or any part of it is threatened by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• Such an emergency can alter the federal structure of the country to a unitary one.
 
 
 
• **Article 356**
 
 
• Article 356, often referred to as President's Rule, deals with the failure of the constitutional machinery in a State.
 
• It allows the President to assume the functions of the State Government and/or to dissolve the State legislative assembly if the State government is unable to function according to the provisions of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 368**
 
 
• Article 368 gives the Parliament the power to amend the Constitution and its procedure.
 
• This power is not absolute and is subject to the judicial review of the Supreme Court.
 
• Amendments can be classified into three categories: simple majority, special majority, and special majority with the ratification of states.
 
• Important amendments include the 42nd Amendment (which brought significant changes to the Constitution) and the 44th Amendment (which restored certain powers to the judiciary and reduced the power of the executive).

questions.question: Which canal has a head regulator capacity of 1133 cumecs (40000 cusecs) and a length of 532 km for which it is considered the world's largest lined irrigation canal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narmada Main Canal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Narmada Main Canal has a head regulator capacity of **1133 cumecs (40000 cusecs)**.
 
• This canal has a total length of **532 km**, making it the **world's largest lined irrigation canal**.
 
• The canal originates from the **Sardar Sarovar Dam** on the Narmada River, located in the Indian state of Gujarat.
 
• The Narmada Main Canal is designed to provide irrigation facilities and drinking water to a large region, including parts of Gujarat, Rajasthan, and even the arid regions of Kutch and Saurashtra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narmada River**

 
 
• The Narmada River is the fifth-largest river in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It flows westwards over a length of 1,312 kilometers before draining into the Arabian Sea.
 
• The river is of immense significance as it serves as a major source of water for irrigation, drinking, and industrial purposes for the states it flows through.
 
 
 
• **Sardar Sarovar Dam**
 
 
• The Sardar Sarovar Dam is one of the largest and most controversial dam projects in India.
 
• It is located on the Narmada River in the state of Gujarat.
 
• The dam is designed to provide water for irrigation, drinking, and industrial purposes to several states including Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan.
 
• The dam has a height of 163 meters and a length of 1,210 meters.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation Canals**
 
 
• Irrigation canals are man-made channels that deliver water to agricultural fields.
 
• These canals are crucial for agriculture, especially in arid and semi-arid regions where rainfall is insufficient.
 
• Lined canals, like the Narmada Main Canal, are constructed with concrete or other materials to prevent water seepage and loss, ensuring efficient water delivery.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the two - sector model?

options.text: The government sector plays an important role.
The economy is considered to be closed.
Firms are the only producing sector in the economy.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The government sector plays an important role.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• In a two-sector model, the economy is simplified to include only two sectors: households and firms.

• There is no foreign sector in a two-sector model, so the economy is considered closed.

• The government sector is not included in a two-sector model, hence it does not play any role.

• Firms are considered the only producing sector in the economy, while households provide factors of production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Two-Sector Model:**

• The two-sector model is a simplified representation of the economy that includes only two sectors: households and firms.

• Households provide factors of production (such as labor, land, and capital) to firms and receive income in return.

• Firms use these factors of production to produce goods and services, which are then sold to households.

• This model assumes that there is no government or foreign sector, making it a closed economy.

• **Closed Economy:**

• A closed economy is one that does not engage in international trade, meaning it does not import or export goods and services.

• All economic activities occur within the domestic borders, and the economy is self-sufficient.

• The two-sector model assumes a closed economy as it does not include a foreign sector.

• **Households and Firms:**

• Households are the owners of factors of production and the consumers of goods and services.

• Firms are the producers of goods and services and the employers of factors of production.

• The interaction between households and firms forms the basis of the two-sector model, highlighting the flow of goods, services, and income between them.

</ul

questions.question: Which concept is related to the disposal of the equity of public sector units in the market for covering the fiscal deficit of the central government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Disinvestment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Disinvestment** refers to the process of selling or liquidating an asset or subsidiary. In the context of public sector units (PSUs), it means the sale of government equity in PSUs.

• Disinvestment is carried out to reduce the fiscal burden on the government and to improve public finances.

• **Quotas**

• A quota is a government-imposed trade restriction that limits the number or value of goods that can be imported or exported during a specified time period.

questions.question: Which of the following methods can be used for liberalisation ?

options.text: Abolishing licensing requirement in most industries
Making procedures for imports and exports tough
Restrictions in fixing the prices of goods and services

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abolishing licensing requirement in most industries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Liberalisation refers to the relaxation of previous government restrictions, usually in areas of social or economic policy.

• Abolishing licensing requirements in most industries makes it easier for businesses to enter the market, thus fostering competition and efficiency.

• This process reduces the bureaucratic hurdles and promotes a more business-friendly environment.

• Liberalisation often leads to increased foreign investment, technological advancement, and overall economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Liberalisation**

• Liberalisation is the process of eliminating unnecessary government control and restrictions in the economy to encourage the free flow of goods and services.

• It typically involves policies such as reducing tariffs, removing quotas, and decreasing subsidies.

• By removing licensing requirements, the government reduces the barriers for new businesses and industries to enter the market.

• This can lead to more dynamic economic activities, as it encourages innovation and competitiveness among businesses.

• **Tax Policies**

• Increasing taxes generally has the opposite effect of liberalisation, as it can discourage investment and economic activity.

• However, tax reforms that lower rates and simplify the tax code can be part of a broader liberalisation strategy.

• **Import and Export Procedures**

• Making procedures for imports and exports more stringent can hinder international trade and economic growth.

• Liberalisation often involves simplifying these procedures to facilitate easier and more efficient cross-border trade.

• **Price Controls**

• Restrictions in fixing the prices of goods and services can distort the market and lead to inefficiencies.

• Removing price controls allows the market to determine prices based on supply and demand, which is a key principle of liberalisation.

</ul

questions.question: Who described India as a ‘Quasi - Federation’?
questions.solution:

__

• KC Wheare was a renowned British constitutional expert and academic.

• He is widely known for his work on federalism and the study of constitutional law.

• Wheare described India as a 'Quasi-Federation' due to its unique blend of federal and unitary features.

• He argued that while India has a federal structure, the central government holds more power compared to other federations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Federalism:**

• Federalism is a system of government where power is divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country.

• In a federal system, the constitution typically provides the division of powers between different levels of government.

• Examples of federal countries include the United States, Canada, Australia, and India.

• **Quasi-Federation:**

• A quasi-federation is a political system that has characteristics of both federal and unitary systems.

• In such a system, the central government may have overarching authority over the constituent units, unlike in a pure federation where the powers of the central and regional governments are more balanced.

• India is often described as a quasi-federation due to the significant powers vested in the central government by the Constitution.

• **Constitution of India:**

• The Constitution of India, adopted in 1950, establishes India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic.

• It lays down the framework for the political principles, structures, procedures, and powers of government institutions.

• It also provides for a federal system with a strong central government, which is why India is often termed a quasi-federation.

• The Constitution includes provisions for both federalism and unitary features, allowing the central government to override state governments under certain circumstances.

</ul

• Vitamin A plays a crucial role in maintaining healthy vision, immune function, and skin health.

• It is a fat-soluble vitamin that is crucial for maintaining vision, promoting growth and development, and protecting epithelium and mucous integrity in the body.

• There are two types of Vitamin A found in nature: preformed Vitamin A (retinol and retinyl ester) and provitamin A carotenoids (beta-carotene, alpha-carotene).

• Preformed Vitamin A is found in foods from animal sources, including dairy products, fish, and meat (especially liver).

• Provitamin A carotenoids are abundant in plant-based foods such as fruits and vegetables, with beta-carotene being the most significant.

• **Beta-carotene**

• It is an antioxidant that gives yellow and orange fruits and vegetables their color.

• In the body, beta-carotene is converted into retinol (Vitamin A), which is necessary for healthy skin, mucous membranes, the immune system, and good eye health and vision.

• Beta-carotene is also known for its role in reducing the risk of chronic diseases by neutralizing free radicals.

• **Sources of Vitamin A**

• Animal sources: Liver, fish oils, milk, eggs.

• Plant sources: Leafy green vegetables (spinach, kale), yellow/orange vegetables (carrots, sweet potatoes), yellow fruits (mangoes, apricots).

• Fortified foods: Some cereals and dairy products are fortified with Vitamin A.

• **Health benefits of Vitamin A**

• Maintains healthy vision and prevents night blindness.

• Supports the immune system by maintaining the integrity and function of skin and mucosal cells.

• Promotes growth and development, especially in children.

• Has antioxidant properties that help in reducing the risk of chronic diseases.
